name: Python
description: Python from syntax and data structures through OOP, idiomatic tools, testing and the NumPy/pandas data stack.

nodes.name: Python basics
nodes.desc: Variables, numbers, booleans, control flow and the interactive interpreter.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write simple Python programs with variables, numbers, booleans and control flow and experiment in the interpreter.

nodes.name: Strings & I/O
nodes.desc: String methods, f-strings, slicing, and reading input and printing output.
nodes.summary: You will be able to manipulate text with string methods, slicing and f-strings and handle console input and output.

nodes.name: Lists, dicts & sets
nodes.desc: The built-in containers, when to use each, and their common operations and costs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between lists, tuples, dicts and sets and use their common operations with an eye on cost.

nodes.name: Functions
nodes.desc: Defining functions, default and keyword arguments, *args/**kwargs, scope and closures.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define flexible functions with default, keyword and variable arguments and understand scope and closures.

nodes.name: Comprehensions
nodes.desc: List, dict and set comprehensions and generator expressions as readable loops.
nodes.summary: You will be able to replace simple loops with list, dict and set comprehensions and generator expressions that stay readable.

nodes.name: Exceptions
nodes.desc: Raising and catching exceptions, custom exception types and when to use them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to raise and handle exceptions, define custom exception types and decide when exceptions are the right tool.

nodes.name: Files & modules
nodes.desc: Reading and writing files, pathlib, importing modules and organising code into packages.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read and write files with pathlib, import modules and organise code into packages.

nodes.name: Classes & objects
nodes.desc: Classes, instances, methods, inheritance and properties in Python.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write Python classes with methods, inheritance and properties to model data and behaviour.

nodes.name: Dunder methods
nodes.desc: Special methods like __repr__, __eq__, __len__ and __iter__ that make objects feel built-in.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement special methods so your objects print, compare, size and iterate like built-in types.

nodes.name: Type hints
nodes.desc: Annotating code with type hints, checking with mypy, and writing dataclasses.
nodes.summary: You will be able to annotate Python code with type hints, check it with mypy and model data with dataclasses.

nodes.name: CLI tool project
nodes.desc: Build a command-line tool with argparse that reads files, handles errors and is split into modules.
nodes.summary: You will build a command-line tool with argparse that reads files, handles errors cleanly and is organised into modules.

nodes.name: Iterators & generators
nodes.desc: The iterator protocol, generators with yield, and lazy pipelines with itertools.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write iterators and generators and build lazy data pipelines with itertools.

nodes.name: Decorators
nodes.desc: Functions as values, writing decorators, functools.wraps and common built-in decorators.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write decorators that wrap functions, preserve metadata with functools.wraps and use common built-in decorators.

nodes.name: Context managers
nodes.desc: The with statement, writing context managers and contextlib.
nodes.summary: You will be able to manage resources with the with statement and write your own context managers with classes or contextlib.
topics: Common uses like files and locks

nodes.name: Concurrency & asyncio
nodes.desc: Threads, processes, the GIL and async/await with asyncio.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between threads, processes and asyncio for concurrent Python code and explain the GIL's effect.

nodes.name: Testing with pytest
nodes.desc: Writing tests, fixtures and parametrised tests with pytest.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write and organise tests with pytest using fixtures and parametrisation.

nodes.name: Packaging & venvs
nodes.desc: Virtual environments, pip, pyproject.toml and publishing a package.
nodes.summary: You will be able to isolate dependencies with virtual environments, configure a project with pyproject.toml and publish a package.

nodes.name: NumPy & pandas
nodes.desc: Vectorised arrays with NumPy and tabular data wrangling with pandas DataFrames.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute with vectorised NumPy arrays and clean, filter and aggregate tabular data with pandas DataFrames.

nodes.name: Plotting
nodes.desc: Charts with matplotlib: line, bar, scatter and histograms from DataFrames.
nodes.summary: You will be able to create line, bar, scatter and histogram charts with matplotlib from DataFrames and label them clearly.

nodes.name: Data analysis project
nodes.desc: Clean a real dataset, summarise it and present findings with charts in a notebook.
nodes.summary: You will clean a real dataset, summarise it and present findings with charts in a notebook.
topics: Writing up conclusions in a notebook
